config.villagerguardgunners.guard_gunner: Villager Guard Gunners Settings
Server-wide settings. Server operators with permission level 4 can change these values. Individual Guard Orders and Quartermaster controls are set in their own inventories.
Enable Combat and Village AI

Enable gun combat, natural gun loadouts, command movement, squad patrols, village discovery, initial guard staffing, automatic defense duties, and Village Armory resupply. Medical treatment, Quartermaster service, and building generation have separate switches.
Automatic Gun Loadouts

One-time gun and ammo loadouts for new guards. Requires Combat and Village AI. This equips guards; Initial Village Guards controls their numbers. Existing guards are not re-equipped when settings change.
Enable Natural Loadouts
Allow eligible newly spawned guards to replace their initial weapon with a datapack-defined TaCZ loadout.
Eligible Spawn Sources
Choose which initial spawn origins can receive automatic loadouts. Only structure spawning is enabled by default.
Replace Crossbows Only
Protect equipment from other mods by replacing only a guard's initial crossbow.
Automatic Gunner Count Radius (blocks)
Radius around each new guard used to count guards with this add-on’s automatic gun loadouts, including recorded guards in unloaded chunks. Manually equipped guards do not count.
Allow Explosive Natural Weapons
Allow datapack pools to issue weapons TaCZ identifies as explosive. All native blast safety remains active.
Easy Difficulty
Normal Difficulty
Hard Difficulty
Squads and Commands
Server-authoritative limits for temporary commands and saved patrol-route execution.
Command Reach (blocks)
Maximum distance from the issuing player to loaded squad members that can receive a command. Farther or unloaded members keep their current orders.
Maximum Affected Guards
Hard limit on authorized squad members changed by one command.
Positional Command Duration (ticks)
Lifetime in ticks for Rally, Defend, Hold, and Fall Back commands. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Focus Target Duration (ticks)
Lifetime in ticks for Focus Target commands. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Defend Radius
Distance guards can move from a Defend command point.
Command Point Distance (blocks)
Distance ahead of you used to choose a command point when you issue Rally, Defend, Hold, or Fall Back while looking into the air.
Follow Saved Squad Patrol Routes

Allow guards to follow routes saved with a Squad Command Ledger. Requires Combat and Village AI. Routes stay saved and editable when this is off. Automatic village patrols and building defense posts use separate switches.
Patrol Movement Speed
Navigation speed modifier while guards follow squad patrol routes. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.
Patrol Waypoint Pause (ticks)
Ticks a guard pauses after reaching a patrol waypoint before continuing. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Patrol Path Failure Limit
Failed or stalled path attempts allowed before a guard skips one unreachable waypoint.
Initial Village Guards

Size the initial guard allowance in new villages. Guard counts and automatic gun loadouts are separate: a village can have more guards than automatically issued guns. Later deaths do not trigger replacement guards.
Scale Initial Guards to Village Size

Size initial guard numbers in new villages, including ordinary villages. Requires Combat and Village AI. Existing villages keep their guards; deaths do not trigger replacements. Spawn sites and Guard Villagers settings can limit the actual count. Off by default.
Minimum Initial Guard Target
Lower limit for the size-based initial target. Must not exceed Maximum Initial Guard Target. Valid spawn sites can limit the actual count. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Maximum Initial Guard Target

Upper limit for initial ordinary guards and building garrisons together. Must be at least Minimum Initial Guard Target. For a zero managed target, set both limits to 0. Does not limit player-created guards. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Residences per Added Guard

Add one to the initial target per this many classified residences, rounded up. Higher values give fewer guards. Later beds do not increase the allowance. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Village Area Cells per Added Guard

Add one to the initial target per this many occupied horizontal 32 × 32 block cells, rounded up. Cells contain classified house or defense-building centers; roads alone do not count. Higher values give fewer guards. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Defense Building Guard Bonus Limit
Maximum added to the initial target by buildings that can generate garrisons, at one guard per building. The maximum village target still applies. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Extra Initial Guards on Hard
Add this many to the initial target on Hard difficulty, within Maximum Initial Guard Target. Other difficulties get no extra bonus. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Additional Residential Template IDs

Count these exact structure template IDs as residences, up to 128 entries. Guard Villagers must also permit guard spawns in those templates. Example: minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_small_house_1. Requires Scale Initial Guards to Village Size.
Village Patrols and Defense

Automatic patrols cover ordinary villages as well as villages with Village Defense Buildings. Fixed defense posts and saved squad routes use separate controls. Readiness durations apply at the next state transition.
Automatic Village Patrols

Send available village residents around outdoor patrol areas, including ordinary villages. Requires Combat and Village AI. Guards need a weapon and at least half health. Manual squads, follow/hold/patrol orders, and other work take priority. Does not spawn or equip guards. Off by default.
Automatic Building Defense Posts

Assign available guards to fixed posts at generated Village Defense Buildings. Requires Combat and Village AI. This is separate from automatic village patrols and saved squad routes. Turning it off preserves saved buildings and orders.
Watch Duration (ticks)
Quiet ticks after a bell before the village returns from Watch to Peace. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Alert Duration (ticks)
Quiet ticks after a confirmed threat before the village enters Recovery. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Village Readiness Recovery Time (ticks)
Quiet time after Alert before the village returns to Peace. This is village readiness, not medical recovery. Existing deadlines keep their starting duration. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Defense Duty Movement Speed
Navigation speed modifier while guards travel to automatic defense posts. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.

config.villagerguardgunners.guard_gunner: Combat
Target acquisition, range, and aiming settings. TaCZ still controls each weapon's statistics.
Base Visibility Delay (ticks)

Base time a guard must see its target before firing. The active tactical profile can add or subtract time; the result stays between 0 and 40 ticks. Setting this to 0 does not remove a profile’s added delay. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Maximum Firing Range
Maximum distance at which a guard can fire, in blocks. TaCZ effective range still controls the guard's preferred combat distance and damage falloff.
Base Combat Retreat Distance (blocks)
Base distance at which the guard tries to retreat from a close target. The active tactical profile multiplies this distance, and explosive guns also require safe blast distance.
Base Aim Tolerance (degrees)

Base allowed aiming error before firing. Smaller values require more precise aim. The active tactical profile multiplies this value; the final tolerance stays between 1 and 45 degrees. This does not change the gun’s spread.
Movement
Navigation behavior while guards are using TaCZ guns
Approach Speed
Navigation speed modifier while approaching a target. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.
Retreat Speed
Navigation speed modifier while retreating from a target that is too close. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.
Reposition Speed
Navigation speed modifier while finding a safe firing lane. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.
Friendly Reposition Delay (ticks)
Ticks before retrying a firing lane blocked by a protected entity. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Weapon-Specific Tactics
Profile selection and guard behavior controls. These settings do not change TaCZ weapon statistics.
Gun-Type Profiles
Map TaCZ gun type labels to tactical profiles. Keys ignore surrounding whitespace and capitalization; conflicting aliases fall back safely.
Per-Gun Profile Overrides
Choose a profile for an exact TaCZ gun ID. Explosive safety cannot be disabled by an override.
Generalist Profile
Skirmisher Profile
Breacher Profile
Marksman Profile
Support Profile
Demolitions Profile
Rules of Engagement
Server-authoritative firing policy applied after Guard Villagers chooses a target.
Engagement Mode
Choose whether guards follow normal Guard Villagers targets, restrict proactive fire to hostile mobs, retaliate defensively, or hold fire.
Defensive Aggression Memory (ticks)
Ticks after an attack during which DEFENSIVE guards can engage the attacker. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Additional Allowed Target Types

Allow these entity types in restricted firing modes if Guard Villagers already selects them as targets. Does not make guards search for them. Hold Fire, target exclusions, and ally protection still take priority. Example: minecraft:zombie.
Never Target These Entity Types

Prevent guards from targeting these entity types with guns. Takes priority over Additional Allowed Target Types. Example: minecraft:creeper. This is a targeting rule, not general protection from stray shots.
config.villagerguardgunners.engagement_m: Permit every non-allied target selected by Guard Villagers' normal AI and configuration.
Fire at selected mobs classified by Minecraft as hostile, such as zombies and skeletons. Other selected types need an Additional Allowed Target Types entry; ally protection still applies.
Fire only at recent attackers of the guard or its protected allies.
Track an otherwise permitted selected target without moving to engage or firing the gun.
config.villagerguardgunners.tactical_pro: Balanced fallback profile matching the established guard behavior.
Mobile close-to-medium-range profile for pistols and submachine guns.
Close-range profile for shotguns and other multi-projectile weapons.
Long-range profile with stricter aim and visibility requirements.
Steady profile for machine guns and sustained fire.
config.villagerguardgunners.guard_gunner: Safety
Friendly-fire clearance settings. Core friendly-fire protection stays active.
Protected-Entity Clearance
Extra clearance around protected entities when validating a shot, in blocks.
Preserve Blocks from Guard Explosions
Prevent guard-owned TaCZ projectile explosions from destroying blocks while retaining their native effects on hostile entities.
Explosive Radius Standoff Multiplier
Multiply the resolved TaCZ explosion radius when calculating the guard's required minimum firing distance.
Additional Explosive Standoff
Additional blocks added after the explosion-radius multiplier when calculating minimum firing distance.
Modpack Ally Protection
Entity tags, explicit type lists, ownership, and team controls shared by every guard-gun safety layer.
Protect Tamed and Owned Mobs
Protect living mobs that have an owner, including pets belonging to other players and compatible modded mobs. Types listed under Remove Ally Protection for These Types are excluded.
Protect Allied Entities
Protect living entities Minecraft considers allied to the guard, including entities on the same scoreboard team.
Additional Protected Entity Types
Namespaced living entity type IDs to protect in addition to the guard_allies datapack tag.
Remove Ally Protection for These Types

Remove protection from the listed entity types, including protection from tags, villager/golem status, ownership, teams, and compatible mods. Guards and the shooter’s owner stay protected. This does not automatically make an entity a target.
Ammo Quality of Life
Nearby pickup and emergency sharing controls. TaCZ remains authoritative for ammo compatibility and reloading.
Pick Up Dropped Ammo
Allow guards to collect compatible TaCZ ammo they naturally walk over without pathfinding to it. Requires the mobGriefing game rule to be on and this guard’s Ammo Pickup order to allow it.
Dropped Ammo Pickup Radius
Maximum passive pickup distance in blocks. Smaller values reduce the area checked around dropped ammo.
Share Ammo Between Guards
Allow a dry guard to request compatible loose ammo from a nearby eligible guard.
Ammo Sharing Radius
Maximum emergency sharing distance in blocks. Searches occur only after a guard runs out of compatible reserve ammo.
Donor Reserve Magazines
Spare ammo a donor keeps after sharing, measured in full magazines for the donor’s gun and attachments. Loaded rounds do not count toward this reserve.
Require Matching Guard Owners
Restrict sharing to guards with the same owner while still allowing two unowned guards to share.
Village Armory Resupply
Automatic ammo resupply from loaded Village Armories. Searches never scan the world or force chunks to load.
Enable Village Armory Resupply
Let otherwise-idle guards with low spare ammo visit accessible Village Armories in loaded chunks. Requires Combat and Village AI. Quartermaster service is configured separately.
Need Check Interval (ticks)
Ticks between staggered ammo-need assessments. Higher values reduce server work but react more slowly. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Armory Search Radius (blocks)
Maximum distance for finding Village Armories in loaded chunks. The search does not load distant chunks.
Armories Checked per Request
Maximum nearby loaded Village Armories checked for one resupply request. A compatible source can be selected from these candidates; Armories beyond this limit are not checked in that search.
Low-Ammo Trigger (magazines)
Request resupply when spare ammo falls below this many magazines for the current gun and attachments. Loaded rounds do not count. 0 disables automatic requests. Must not exceed Target Spare Ammo.
Target Spare Ammo (magazines)

Desired spare ammo after resupply, measured in magazines using the guard’s current gun and attachments. Must be at least Low-Ammo Trigger. A lower value stops automatic Armory resupply. Loaded rounds are not spare ammo.
Resupply Movement Speed
Navigation speed used only while travelling toward an already-reserved Village Armory. A speed factor: 1 uses the guard’s normal movement speed, 0.5 uses half. This is not blocks per second.
Request Lifetime (ticks)
Maximum lifetime in ticks of one active ammo request. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Reservation Lifetime (ticks)
Maximum time in ticks that one guard can reserve a specific Armory supply slot. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Success Cooldown (ticks)
Delay in ticks after a successful withdrawal before the guard can reassess Armory need. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
No-Supply Retry Delay (ticks)
Delay in ticks after no compatible loaded Village Armory can be selected. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Unreachable Retry Delay (ticks)
Base delay in ticks after a guard cannot reach a reserved Village Armory. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Standalone Village Watchtowers

Controls separate Watchtower structures in newly generated terrain. Village-integrated Watchtowers are controlled under Village Defense Buildings. Datapacks set placement frequency, guard groups, and starting stock.
Generate Standalone Watchtowers
Allow new standalone Village Watchtowers in newly generated terrain. Existing towers and already selected structure starts are preserved. Village-integrated Watchtowers use a separate switch.
Spawn Watchtower Guards
Allow guard markers in newly placed Watchtower pieces to create Guard Villagers.
Maximum Guards per Post
Maximum guards created from one Watchtower guard marker, from 0 through 4.
Place Watchtower Armories
Allow Armory markers in newly placed Watchtower pieces to create Village Armories.
Stock Watchtower Armories
Allow newly generated Watchtower Armories to receive their datapack-defined initial ammo stock.
Watchtower Gun Chance Multiplier

Multiply each new Watchtower guard's normal difficulty-based gun chance once, then clamp the result to 100%. This does not bypass loadout eligibility, nearby caps, datapack pools, inventory limits, or weapon safety. 1 = the base chance; 1.5 = one and a half times that chance. 0 prevents these gun upgrades.
Village Defense Buildings
Add defense buildings to newly generated villages. Layout switches require reopening the world or restarting the server. Standalone Watchtowers use separate settings; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Village Defense Buildings

Add enabled defense building types to supported villages. Off by default so you can choose whether to extend village generation. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Barracks
Allow Barracks when Generate Village Defense Buildings is on. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Village Armory Buildings

Allow Village Armory Buildings when Generate Village Defense Buildings is on. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Sentry Posts
Allow Sentry Posts when Generate Village Defense Buildings is on. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Village-Integrated Watchtowers

Allow Village-Integrated Watchtowers when Generate Village Defense Buildings is on. Standalone Watchtowers use a separate switch. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Generate Training Yards
Allow Training Yards when Generate Village Defense Buildings is on. Reopen the world or restart the server for layout changes. Affects newly generated villages; existing villages are preserved.
Spawn Village Garrison Guards
Allow newly generated Barracks, Sentry Posts, integrated Watchtowers, and Training Yards to create one limited guard group. Existing buildings are never staffed retroactively.
Maximum Guards per Building
Global ceiling from 0 through 4. Sentry Posts remain limited to 1 guard; integrated Watchtowers and Training Yards remain limited to 2.
Village Garrison Gun Chance Multiplier

Multiply each new village-garrison guard's difficulty-based gun chance once, then clamp it to 100%. Natural-loadout population, datapack, inventory, and safety gates still apply. 1 = the base chance; 1.5 = one and a half times that chance. 0 prevents these gun upgrades.
Place Village Armory Storage Blocks
Place a public Village Armory storage block inside each new Armory building. Requires Generate Village Defense Buildings. Existing buildings are preserved.
Stock Village Armories
Fill newly generated village Armories once from their configured datapack loot table. Disabling this still places an empty Armory.
Advanced Performance
Scheduling controls. Lower intervals react faster but require more server work.
Visibility Sample Interval (ticks)
Ticks between target visibility samples. Lower values react faster but use more CPU. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Movement Decision Interval (ticks)
Ticks between combat movement decisions. Lower values react faster but use more CPU. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Path Recalculation Interval (ticks)
Ticks between navigation path recalculations. Lower values respond faster to changes but use more CPU. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Gun Data Refresh Interval (ticks)
Ticks between cached TaCZ gun-data refreshes. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Blocked-Shot Recheck Delay (ticks)

Time a guard can reuse a blocked-shot result before checking again. Higher values reduce repeated checks but can delay firing after the obstruction clears. 0 keeps reuse within the same tick. Safety checks remain active. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Reposition Progress Interval (ticks)
A guard stops and replans after twice this duration without route progress, with a minimum of 20 ticks. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.

Chance for a new guard to receive a gun loadout: 0 = 0%, 0.5 = 50%, 1 = 100%. The nearby automatic-gunner cap, spawn-source rules, and available loadout pool still apply.
Maximum Nearby Automatic Gunners
Maximum guards with automatic gun loadouts within Automatic Gunner Count Radius. Set to 0 to disable automatic loadouts for this difficulty. This is not a cap on all guards or manually supplied guns.
Gun Loadout Pool ID
Datapack loadout pool for this difficulty, such as villagerguardgunners:normal. Use a namespaced pool ID; missing or invalid pools leave the guard’s starting equipment unchanged.
Preferred Distance Multiplier
Multiply the gun’s TaCZ effective range to choose an approach distance. 1 = unchanged, 0.5 = half, 2 = double. The result stays within the guard’s retreat and maximum firing distances.
Combat Retreat Distance Multiplier
Multiply Base Combat Retreat Distance. 1 = unchanged, 2 = double. Explosive blast clearance can require more distance; non-explosive movement stays within the firing limit.
Visibility Delay Adjustment (ticks)
Add to or subtract from Base Visibility Delay. Positive values delay firing; negative values shorten the delay. The final delay stays between 0 and 40 ticks. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Aim Tolerance Multiplier
Multiply Base Aim Tolerance. Smaller values require more precise aim; 0.5 halves the allowed error. Final tolerance stays between 1 and 45 degrees. Does not change gun spread.
Use Effective-Range Firing Limit
Also limit firing distance using TaCZ effective range instead of only the global hard cap.
Effective Firing Range Multiplier
Multiply TaCZ effective range when Use Effective-Range Firing Limit is on. Has no effect while that option is off. 1 = unchanged, 2 = double; the server and individual guard firing caps still apply.

Treat injured guards and optionally rescue downed guards. Server permissions below work together with each guard’s Medic Duty and Medical Retreat controls. Timings affect new treatment actions; ongoing actions keep their starting duration.
Allow manual treatment and medic care. Supplies remain accessible when this is off. Disabling treatment moves existing downed or stabilized guards into recovery.
Allow guards with Medic Duty on to treat nearby allied guards. Requires Enable Medical Treatment and supplies in the medic’s pouch. Each guard starts with Medic Duty off.

Allow guards with Medical Retreat on to seek a safe medic at 35% health or less and resume normal behavior at 75%. Requires Medical Treatment and Medic Duty to be allowed. Individual guards start with retreat off; player movement orders take priority.
Enable Downed Guards

Allow two-dose rescue after lethal injuries: the first dose stabilizes and the second revives. Requires Medical Treatment and valid treatment supplies. Some damage bypasses downing. Off by default; disabling it moves existing casualties into recovery.
Enable Cot Care and Transport

Enable cot and field revival timings below. Requires Medical Treatment and Downed Guards. Carrying additionally requires Medic Duty to be allowed, a supplied medic, a free nearby Recovery Cot, and a usable route. Manual revival remains available when medic AI is off.
Cot Revival Treatment Time (ticks)

Time for the second dose to revive a stabilized guard on a Recovery Cot. Default: 40 ticks = 2 seconds. Requires Medical Treatment, Downed Guards, and Cot Care and Transport. Does not change ordinary healing or the first stabilization dose. Travel, assessment, and dose cooldowns add time. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Field Revival Treatment Time (ticks)

Time for the second dose to revive a stabilized guard away from a cot. Default: 160 ticks = 8 seconds. Uses the larger of this value and Cot Revival Treatment Time. Requires Medical Treatment, Downed Guards, and Cot Care and Transport. Does not change ordinary healing or the first stabilization dose. Travel, assessment, and dose cooldowns add time. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Rest After Cot Revival (ticks)

Rest after revival on a Recovery Cot before returning to duty; this is not time to full health. Default: 100 ticks = 5 seconds. A blocked exit can extend the stay. Requires Medical Treatment, Downed Guards, and Cot Care and Transport. Does not change ordinary healing or the first stabilization dose. Travel, assessment, and dose cooldowns add time. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
Rest After Field Revival (ticks)

Rest after revival away from a cot before returning to duty; this is not time to full health. Default: 400 ticks = 20 seconds. Uses the larger of this value and Rest After Cot Revival. Requires Medical Treatment, Downed Guards, and Cot Care and Transport. Does not change ordinary healing or the first stabilization dose. Travel, assessment, and dose cooldowns add time. 20 ticks = 1 second at normal game speed.
